title: He knows what your own self whispers to you.
subtitle: Nearer than the vein in your neck
then: Allah affirms He created man and {idea}knows every thought that crosses his mind,{/idea} good or bad. Ibn Kathir explains the nearness as His angels, by His leave, being closer than the jugular vein. He also brings the hadith that {reward}Allah forgives the Ummah what they think to themselves as long as they do not say or do it.{/reward}
now: Three in the morning, you cannot sleep, and the same anxious loop runs in your head. No one in the house knows. {idea}He does, every word of it.{/idea} That is not only a warning. It means you are never talking to an empty room.
old: No one knows what goes on inside my head.
new: Allah knows my inner whispers better than I do, and that makes Him the first one to talk to about them.
try: Tonight, put the thought that keeps looping into a quiet dua, word for word.

title: Two recorders, one on the right, one on the left.
subtitle: The angels who receive every deed
then: After His own knowledge, Allah mentions {idea}the two receiving angels{/idea} seated on the right and the left of every person. Ibn Kathir says they receive and record deeds, citing 82:10-12: {idea}honorable scribes who know what you do.{/idea}
now: You are alone in a hotel room on a work trip, no one you know for a hundred miles. It feels like a pause from being watched. {idea}Your two companions came with you.{/idea} They also write down the quiet good you do when no one is around.
old: When I am far from people who know me, it does not really count.
new: Two honorable recorders are always seated with me, writing the good as well as the rest.
try: Next time you are alone, do one small good deed on purpose and remember it is written.

title: Not one word leaves your mouth unrecorded.
subtitle: The weight of a single sentence

row.title: one word, His pleasure
sub: or His anger, till the Day

then: Every word is noted by a watcher ready to record it. The Prophet ﷺ said a man may speak a word that pleases Allah without realizing its reach, and {reward}Allah writes His pleasure for him until he meets Him.{/reward} The same is true of a word that angers Him. Alqamah said: how many words have I left unsaid because of this hadith.
now: A voice note to a friend about your boss. A sharp reply in the comments. A kind word to the cleaner at work you almost did not say. {idea}All of it is written.{/idea} {reward}So is the encouragement you give your child at bedtime.{/reward}
old: Words are cheap, it is actions that count.
new: A single word can carry Allah's pleasure or anger to the Day I meet Him.
try: Before sending your next message today, read it once as if it will be shown to you on the Day.

title: Death arrives with the truth you were avoiding.
subtitle: The one appointment no one escapes
then: Ibn Kathir explains this as the end people try to escape, {trap}now arriving with no shelter from it.{/trap} Even the Prophet ﷺ, wiping sweat from his face at death, said: {idea}Glory be to Allah, death has its stupor.{/idea}
now: You change the subject when your parents talk about their will. You skip the janazah because it makes you uneasy. {idea}Avoiding the thought does not move the date.{/idea} Preparing for it is gentler than being surprised by it.
old: If I do not think about death, I can enjoy life more.
new: Death is coming whether I look at it or not, and facing it now makes my life more honest.
try: Attend the next janazah you hear of, or visit a graveyard this week and make dua for the people there.

title: The Trumpet is blown: the promised Day has come.
subtitle: After death, the next step of the journey
then: The Prophet ﷺ said: how can I feel at ease when the angel of the Trumpet has put it to his mouth, waiting for the command? His Companions asked what they should say. He ﷺ told them: {reward}Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs.{/reward}
now: Bad news on the phone, a scan result, a layoff email. Your heart races. {reward}The words the Companions were taught for the Trumpet work for every smaller fear too.{/reward} Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil.
old: Thinking about the Day only makes me afraid.
new: The Prophet ﷺ answered that fear with trust: Allah is enough for us.
try: Memorize Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil today and say it the next time you feel afraid.

title: Every soul arrives with a driver and a witness.
subtitle: No one walks to the reckoning alone
then: Uthman bin Affan recited this verse in a speech and explained it: {idea}a driver to lead each person to Allah, and a witness to testify to what he did.{/idea} Ibn Jarir preferred this meaning, as Ibn Kathir reports.
now: At work you can explain away a missed deadline, spin the story, blame the printer. {trap}That Day there is no spin.{/trap} {idea}The witness was there the whole time.{/idea} So today is the day to live a story you would not need to explain.
old: I can always explain myself later.
new: A witness will speak for what I did, so I would rather act well now than explain later.
try: Own one small mistake today, out loud, without an excuse.

title: The cover is lifted, and now your sight is sharp.
subtitle: Seeing clearly when it is too late to change
then: On that Day {idea}everyone's sight becomes clear and strong,{/idea} even those who denied. Ibn Kathir notes this sight will not help them then, citing 32:12 where they beg to be sent back to do good. {trap}The cover of heedlessness was the real problem.{/trap}
now: Endless scrolling, back-to-back shows, a calendar so full you never sit still. {trap}Life can be one long covering.{/trap} {reward}The clear sight is on offer today too, in a quiet moment with the Quran.{/reward}
old: One day I will see things clearly and sort myself out.
new: The clear sight will come either way, and it only helps me if it comes before the Day.
try: Sit for five minutes today with no phone, no noise, and ask yourself what you would change if you saw clearly.

title: Here is the record, ready, nothing added or missing.
subtitle: The companion angel presents the file
then: The angel who recorded every deed now testifies. Ibn Kathir says it is {idea}prepared and completed without addition or deletion.{/idea} This is when Allah judges creation with fairness.
now: Your bank statement at the end of the month, every transaction listed, the ones you forgot too. {idea}A record like that, but for your whole life.{/idea} {reward}You can still add good entries tonight.{/reward}
old: Most of what I did is forgotten by now.
new: My record is exact and fair, and I am still writing it today.
try: Add one good entry before you sleep tonight: a charity, a call to a parent, a prayer on time.

title: Every stubborn rejecter of truth is cast out.
subtitle: Stubbornness against what you know is true
then: Allah commands the driver and witness angels to cast into Hell {trap}every stubborn disbeliever.{/trap} Ibn Kathir describes him as one who {trap}stubbornly rejected the truth, knowingly contradicting it with falsehood.{/trap}
now: Someone shows you, kindly, that you were wrong in an argument. You know it. You still dig in, because backing down feels like losing. {idea}That stubborn streak is worth softening while it is small.{/idea}
old: Admitting I am wrong makes me look weak.
new: Knowing the truth and refusing it is the real danger, so giving in to truth is strength.
try: Admit you were wrong about one thing today, to someone who will notice.

title: Blocking good, crossing limits, spreading doubt.
subtitle: Three habits that describe the stubborn one
then: Ibn Kathir explains each word. {trap}Preventer of good:{/trap} he did not keep family ties or give charity. {trap}Aggressor:{/trap} Qatadah said, in speech, behavior and affairs. {trap}Doubter:{/trap} he doubts, and raises doubts in others.
now: A cousin asks for help with rent and you say no without thinking. A colleague wants to start praying at work and you joke that it is pointless. {idea}These are small versions of big traits.{/idea} Turn each one around while it is easy.
old: Not helping is neutral, I am not hurting anyone.
new: Holding back good and planting doubt are deeds too, and their opposite is open to me today.
try: Do the opposite of one trait today: give something, speak gently, or encourage someone's faith.

title: He set up another god beside Allah.
subtitle: The root beneath every other trait
then: The list of traits ends with the root of them all: {trap}associating others with Allah and worshipping others besides Him.{/trap} Ibn Kathir brings a hadith naming three the Fire is entrusted with: the stubborn tyrant, the one who sets up another god, and the one who kills unjustly.
now: No statues in your house. But you check the market at dawn before your prayer, or fear your boss more than Allah. {idea}Worship is about what gets first place in your heart.{/idea} Keep that place for Him alone.
old: Shirk is something ancient people did with idols.
new: Worship belongs to Allah alone, and I keep watch over what I put first.
try: Tomorrow morning, make your first act of the day a remembrance of Allah, before the phone.

title: His devil says: I did not make him do it.
subtitle: The companion who walks away at the end
then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said this companion is {trap}the devil assigned to every person.{/trap} On the Day he will disown the man completely. Ibn Kathir links it to 14:22, where Shaytan says: I only called you and you answered, {trap}so blame yourselves.{/trap}
now: You tell yourself it was the whispers, the mood, the friend group. The voice that tempted you will not stand by you later. {idea}It will be the first to say it was all your choice.{/idea} Which also means the choice is still yours now.
old: Shaytan pushed me, it was not really my fault.
new: He only invites; I am the one who says yes or no, today and that Day.
try: When a familiar temptation comes today, say A'udhu billah out loud and walk away from it once.

title: Do not argue before Me; the warning came long ago.
subtitle: The time to dispute is over
then: As the man and his devil companion blame each other, Allah stops them: {trap}do not dispute before Me.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains: I gave you enough proof through the messengers, sent down Books, and {idea}established the signs before you.{/idea}
now: This verse is part of the warning it describes. You are reading it now, on a screen, years before that Day. {idea}The argument you might make later, I did not know, is being answered today.{/idea}
old: If I really knew, I would have done better.
new: The warning has reached me, here and now, so the time to respond is now too.
try: Act today on one thing you have learned from the Quran this week.

title: His word does not change, and He wrongs no one.
subtitle: A judgment that is final and perfectly fair
then: Allah closes the exchange: {idea}My word will not be changed,{/idea} Mujahid said, I have made My decision. Then {reward}I am not unjust to the servants.{/reward} Ibn Kathir explains He punishes no one except for their sins after proof has been established.
now: You have been treated unfairly: a promotion that went to someone else, a family decision that ignored you. {reward}There is one court where no one is ever wronged.{/reward} {idea}That is a comfort and a call to be fair yourself.{/idea}
old: Life is unfair, and in the end it may stay that way.
new: Allah never wrongs anyone, so final justice is certain, for me and from me.
try: Make one decision today with someone else's fairness in mind, even if it costs you a little.

title: Hell is asked: are you full? It says: is there more?
subtitle: A fire that is never satisfied, and a Paradise with room
then: Ibn Kathir explains the apparent meaning: {trap}Hell will keep asking if there are any more.{/trap} In the hadiths he brings, Allah tells Paradise: {reward}you are My mercy, with which I show mercy to whom I will,{/reward} and Paradise has space left over until He creates others to fill it. He wrongs no one.
now: There are things in your life that never say enough: a craving, a habit, an appetite for more likes. {trap}That hunger is a small picture of this verse.{/trap} {reward}And Paradise is so wide there is room to spare. Ask for it.{/reward}
old: Talk of Hell just makes me feel hopeless.
new: The Fire is never satisfied, but Paradise is Allah's mercy with room to spare, so I turn toward it.
try: Ask Allah for Paradise by name in your next prayer, three times.
